findings.issue_category: hard-coded AWS credentials in user data
findings.description: The user_data script exports a long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key in cleartext. EC2 user data is readable by any process on the host or via SSRF against 169.254.169.254/latest/user-data, and the keys are also committed to source control.

Ingress allows TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0 on a security group attached to an instance in a public subnet with an internet gateway route, exposing the management port to the entire internet for brute-force and exploit attempts.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and no TLS listener or certificate exists anywhere in the configuration, so portal traffic is served in cleartext and is subject to interception or tampering.

Egress permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing no outbound segmentation and easing data exfiltration or command-and-control callbacks from a compromised host that holds the embedded credentials.
The EBS data volume attached at /dev/sdh does not set encrypted = true and specifies no KMS key, so its contents are stored unencrypted.
The snapshot is derived from an unencrypted EBS volume and therefore inherits unencrypted status, persisting plaintext data in an artifact that can be copied or shared across accounts.

No metadata_options block is specified, so the instance defaults to token-optional IMDSv1. On an internet-facing web server this makes SSRF a direct path to reading user data (including the embedded keys) and any role credentials.

The instance is launched into a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch = true that routes 0.0.0.0/0 to an internet gateway, giving it direct internet reachability with no load balancer, NAT, or bastion boundary.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is declared, so the root EBS volume - which will hold the credentials injected via user data - may be stored unencrypted depending on account defaults.
The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, leaving sensitive network telemetry stored without enforced encryption or customer-managed key control.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, ACL, or bucket policy accompanies the flow log bucket, so nothing prevents a public ACL or policy from later exposing network flow records.
The bucket has no policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, permitting flow log objects to be written or retrieved over unencrypted HTTP.

findings.issue_category: force destroy on audit log bucket
findings.description: force_destroy = true allows the flow log bucket and all stored network audit records to be deleted in a single destroy operation, undermining log integrity and forensic retention.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true means every instance placed in this subnet automatically receives a public IP, defaulting workloads to internet exposure rather than explicit opt-in.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true makes this subnet public by default, so any future workload placed here is directly internet-reachable without explicit opt-in.
No aws_default_security_group resource restricts the VPC's default security group, so it remains unmanaged with its implicit allow-all intra-group rules for any resource that falls back to it.
